default.q.test-1-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 見かけた
The transitive verb 見かける means to happen to see or catch sight of someone, and correctly combines with the particle を to describe accidentally seeing someone pass by.
default.q.test-1-q1-1.explanation: The verb 見かける has the structure 「[person/thing] を見かける」 and describes accidentally catching sight of someone or something briefly, without arranging to meet or directly interacting. Thus, 「昨日、駅で木村さんを見かけた。」means: “Yesterday, I happened to see Kimura-san at the station.” Another example is 「今朝、通勤途中で田中さんを見かけた。」 (This morning, I happened to see Tanaka-san on my way to work.) To avoid confusion, remember that 会う must be used with the particle に (〜に会う) and implies meeting or interacting, whereas 見かける takes を (〜を見かける) and simply means to catch sight of someone.
default.q.test-1-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) 会う (to meet) takes the particle に, as in 木村さんに会った, not the particle を.
default.q.test-1-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) 見物する means to visit or view a sight, and is used for places or events, not for people.
default.q.test-1-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) のぞく means to peek, look through a gap, or drop by a place, so it does not fit the meaning here.
default.q.test-1-q1-1.why.3: ✓ (d) 見かける is a transitive verb used with the particle を, meaning to happen to see or catch sight of someone.

The complete sentence means: “Polka-dot clothes have been very fashionable recently.” Distinguish 「模様」(a pattern on a material) from 「無地」(plain, without a pattern) and 「絵」(an independent picture or drawing). default.q.test-1-q10-10.why.3: ✓ (d) 「模様」(moyō) means “pattern” or “design”; combined with 「水玉」, it forms 「水玉模様」, meaning a polka-dot pattern.
default.q.test-1-q2-2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 持ち帰り
In Japan’s food-service industry, 「お持ち帰りですか」 is a fixed honorific expression asking whether a customer would like the food to take away. It forms the natural contrast with 「こちらでお召し上がりですか」 (“Will you eat here?”).
default.q.test-1-q2-2.explanation: In Japanese customer service and hospitality (接客), staff use honorific language in patterns such as 「お + noun / verb stem + ですか」 to ask customers about their wishes politely. In this context, the noun 「持ち帰り」(from the verb 持ち帰る, to take home) combines with the prefix 「お」 as a fixed expression for takeout, corresponding to the honorific expression 「お召し上がり」(the honorific form of 食べる/飲む). The complete sentence means: "Would you like to eat here or take it to go?" A similar everyday example is: 「お持ち帰りのご注文はあちらのレジで承ります。」(For takeout orders, please place your order at the register over there.) The distinction depends on the compound that follows: 「〜帰り」 means taking something all the way back to one's own place, 「〜出し」 means taking something out of a storage area, 「〜歩き」 means carrying something while walking, and 「〜運び」 refers to transporting or carrying an object.

default.q.test-1-q2-2.why.1: ✗ (b) 持ち出し means taking documents or objects out of a designated place or workplace, and is not used for food or drinks taken away.
default.q.test-1-q2-2.why.2: ✗ (c) 持ち歩き means “carrying something around while walking or traveling,” not buying food to take home.
default.q.test-1-q2-2.why.3: ✗ (d) 持ち運び means “carrying or transporting things,” often emphasizing convenience and portability; it is not a term for serving a dish.

To connect an -i adjective to another adjective, change the ending to「～くて」(こい → こくて). default.q.test-10-q1-1.verdict:

The phrase 「コストを下げる」 means “cut costs / reduce production costs,” the most direct and important measure for improving a product’s competitiveness.
default.q.test-10-q1-1.explanation: In business Japanese, 「コストを下げる」 (or 「コストを削減する」) is a fixed expression meaning to optimize input and operating expenses in order to lower the cost of a product. Combined with the necessary conditional pattern 「～ないと、…ない」 (“if we do not..., we cannot...”), the sentence emphasizes the urgency of reducing costs to achieve the desired result. The completed sentence means: “If we do not cut costs further, we will not be able to compete successfully with our rivals’ products.” Another example is: 「生産工程を見直して、徹底的にコストを下げる。」 (“Review the production process and reduce costs thoroughly.”) For the N2, clearly distinguish 「コスト」 (the actual expenses that make up a product’s price) from 「予算」 (a budget limit allocated in advance). To lower a product’s market price and compete directly, use 「コスト」.

default.q.test-10-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) 「資本」means business capital or capital funds, and does not combine with 「下げる」in the context of competing over product prices.
default.q.test-10-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) 「利益」 means profit, which is a business goal to increase, not something deliberately lowered in order to compete.
default.q.test-10-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) 「予算」means a budget planned for a project and usually combines with 「削る」or 「抑える」; it is not used to refer to the cost of producing a product.
